faq.q: Why does social media make me feel bad about myself?
faq.a: You see other people's best moments and compare them with your everyday life, including your bad days. That unfair comparison can make you feel you are not good enough.
asks: Why do I feel worse after Instagram?

faq.q: Are photos on social media real?
faq.a: Many are not the full truth. People often take lots of photos, choose the best, and use filters or editing apps to change faces, bodies and backgrounds.

faq.q: How do I stop comparing myself to others?
faq.a: Remind yourself you are seeing highlights. Compare yourself with your past self, unfollow accounts that make you feel bad, and spend more time on real-life friends and hobbies.
asks: How do I feel happy with myself?

faq.q: What age can I use social media?
faq.a: Most big social media apps say users must be at least 13 years old. Talk with your family about which apps are right for you and how to stay safe.
asks: How old do you have to be for social media?

faq.q: What if someone posts something mean about me?
faq.a: Do not reply. Save a screenshot, block and report the person, and tell a trusted grown-up straight away. It is never your fault.
asks: Someone posted a mean comment about me

facts: Most big social media apps, such as Instagram and TikTok, require users to be at least 13 years old.
In 1954, psychologist Leon Festinger described "social comparison", our natural habit of judging ourselves by comparing with others.
